title: Kernels of quasi-coherent modules on the small etale site of a scheme
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(u:U\to T)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] such that $M$ and $N$ are quasi-coherent in the sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Then the kernel $\ker\varphi$ in the category of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules, given on each object $U$ of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ by $(\ker\varphi)(U)=\ker(\varphi_U:M(U)\to N(U))$, is quasi-coherent in the sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

source.place: Tag 0GNB (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), part (3), and its proof via Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), parts (1) and (5): F -> F^a is fully faithful and exact into Mod(S_etale, O). Algebraic-space version: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (3).

proof.text: Restrict M and N to quasi-coherent Zariski modules F and G using the specified restriction functor in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], and let f be the restriction of phi. The counit is an isomorphism at M and N and its naturality identifies the extension of f with phi. The same theorem supplies natural section isomorphisms from the extension of every quasi-coherent Zariski module H to U |-> Gamma(U,u^*H), including compatibility with every morphism used below.

source.place: Tag 0GNB(3), via the left-exactness argument of Tag 06VE(5).

proof.text: Let K=ker(f) with inclusion i. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], K is quasi-coherent. Its etale extension is therefore quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Restriction is additive directly on components, so its left adjoint extension is additive and the extended kernel pair is a short complex.

source.place: Tag 0GNB(3), via the left-exactness argument of Tag 06VE(5).

proof.text: For an etale object u:U->T, etaleness implies flatness ([def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism]). The tensor pullback is additive by its adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], and preserves finite limits by the already proved [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective]. Thus it preserves the kernel fork of f. Global sections preserve that kernel fork by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. The resulting section complex Gamma(U,u^*K)->Gamma(U,u^*F)->Gamma(U,u^*G) is exact with monic first arrow.

source.place: Tag 0GNB(3), via the left-exactness argument of Tag 06VE(5).

proof.text: The section isomorphisms and morphism compatibility from [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identify the evaluated extended complex with the complex of Step 3. Transport exactness and monicity through this isomorphism. Object evaluations jointly reflect limits of presheaves, and forgetting a sheaf of modules to its additive presheaf reflects limits, as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. Hence the extended inclusion is a categorical kernel of the extended f. Uniqueness of kernels and the counit isomorphisms of Step 1 identify the extension of K with ker(phi). Quasi-coherence is invariant under this isomorphism; sheafification on each slice is available by the equivalence of the etale slice over U and the small etale site of U. Finally evaluation of the actual kernel fork of phi preserves its limit, giving injectivity and Function.Exact on every object as asserted.
